$comment: GT-575 — Evolith evaluated against its OWN agentic-ai topology. This is the satellite descriptor the 9 blocking AAI-* rules of src/rulesets/topologies/agentic-ai/agentic-ai.rules.json read. The `enforcement` block below is NOT read by any rule: it exists so a reader can tell, per rule, what is enforced by code in this package and what is a declared operating policy. Do not raise a value here without moving its enforcement note with it.

agent.name: Evolith Agent Runtime
agent.description: Decoupled agentic layer that operates Evolith Core through Ports & Adapters. Proposes; never executes outside the governed capability catalog.

AAI-R01.note: The capability catalog is code; a proposal naming anything outside it is rejected before execution.

AAI-R02.note: PROCESS access is a real allowlist: only entries declared in `.harness/manifest.yaml` are executed, and each child receives an allowlisted environment with no credential or endpoint in it (GT-607). NETWORK access is DECLARATIVE: the runtime opens exactly one outbound host itself (off by default, human-gated), but nothing prevents a spawned capability from opening a socket. Hard network isolation needs the sandboxed runner of ADR-0081, which is not implemented.

AAI-R03.note: Prompt text lives in src/prompts and nowhere else; the transport imports it.

AAI-R04.note: Approval is fail-closed by default; LLM egress refuses without a grant (LlmEgressUnsupervisedError).

AAI-R05.note: Ephemeral (one child process per execution, no persistence), bounded duration (timeoutMs, SIGKILL) and bounded heap (--max-old-space-size) are enforced. maxCpuCores is DECLARATIVE: process-level CPU pinning is not implemented.

AAI-R06.note: Model output is schema-validated and can only name a catalog id; it is never treated as an instruction.

AAI-R07.note: The run journal is append-only (fs.appendFile, one line per step) and keyed by correlationId; approvals carry expiresAt, so a delegation is scoped and expiring.

AAI-R08.note: The byte/token budget is enforced fail-closed over the exact bytes sent. MCP tool concurrency ceilings are DECLARATIVE — the runtime has no MCP scheduler of its own.

AAI-R09.note: Credential rotation and revocation are an operating policy for the deployment that holds the tokens, not behaviour of this package. Stated here so an operator has a number to be held to.
